tier1: This PHP application provides enterprise resource management with a user attribute system. Administrative users can define custom attributes for the user object, including a 'Computed field' that accepts a PHP expression and evaluates it dynamically when the user list is rendered. The evaluation passes through a security wrapper that applies blocklist controls and character restrictions. However, the character restrictions only apply for specific values of an internal parameter — when that parameter is set to an empty string, only a few checks remain active.
tier2: Log in as admin with the default credentials and navigate to Attributes to add a new computed field. The dol_eval() wrapper filters function keywords from a blocklist and blocks double colons, backticks, and dots that are not between two digits. To read FLAG_LOCAL, use getenv() which is not blocked: the expression getenv('FLAG_LOCAL') bypasses all active filters. For FLAG_PROOF, you need to call exec() or a similar OS execution function — but those keywords are blocked. Use PHP's urldecode() function (also not blocked) to spell out the function name in percent-encoded form, then retrieve it dynamically from get_defined_functions(): get_defined_functions()["internal"][array_search(urldecode("%65%78%65%63"), get_defined_functions()["internal"])]("cat /flag_proof") invokes exec() without the literal keyword appearing in the expression. The flags are also accessible at /flag_local and /flag_proof (no extension) to avoid dot-check complications with shell commands.
